item.title: US-led consortium agrees to acquire assets from Russian oil company Lukoil
item.description: A consortium led by Eldridge is set to acquire the international energy assets of Lukoil, a Russian oil company. This move occurs as Lukoil seeks to divest from its global portfolio in light of U.S. sanctions. The acquisition includes non-Russian energy assets spanning multiple countries and significant production capabilities. Concerns have arisen regarding the involvement of the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation in the deal.

item.title: Four oil tankers catch fire after hitting naval mines in Strait of Hormuz: Iran
item.description: Four oil tankers exploded and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz after striking naval mines. The Iranian Navy reported that two vessels had entered a restricted area, disabling their identification systems. Tanker operators are being warned against unauthorized routes due to the risk of explosions. Concurrently, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations noted that three vessels were struck by unidentified projectiles.

item.title: Keralam seeks Centre's help as oil firms refuse ethanol-free petrol samples
item.description: Keralam's government has asked for the Centre's help in acquiring necessary ethanol-free petrol samples. State officials are concerned about ethanol's impact on automobile engines amid rising complaints. The request follows failed attempts to obtain necessary samples from oil companies for verification. Inspections were initiated after allegations of excess ethanol content in petrol surfaced in Karnataka. The state aims to ensure compliance with permissible ethanol limits in petrol distribution.

item.title: China, India set for record Russian oil imports in 2026, but demand seen peaking
item.description: China and India are set to achieve record imports of Russian oil due to supply gaps. This increase comes amid the ongoing Iran war and US sanctions waivers affecting oil purchases. Chinese imports have risen significantly, accounting for about a quarter of its total oil imports. India's imports also surged, with expectations that demand will stabilize as Middle Eastern supplies normalize.

item.title: Petrol, diesel prices rose 7% in India vs 50-70% globally over four years: Hardeep Puri
item.description: Union Minister Hardeep Singh Puri announced that fuel prices in India have risen by just 7% over four years. The government implemented three reductions in central excise duty, helping maintain stable prices. Puri criticized rumors of an LPG shortage, emphasizing increased domestic production of LPG. Challenges from international conflicts and geopolitical tensions still persist, affecting the crude oil market.
